disclaimer: Recommendations follow site SOPs. In an emergency, follow your site's emergency procedures and call the emergency team first.

FIRE.text: Raise the fire alarm and call the emergency team / fire brigade.
Evacuate everyone from the area by the nearest safe exit to the assembly point.
Do not use lifts; use the stairs.
Use the correct extinguisher only if the fire is small and you are trained (CO2 for electrical fires).
Isolate electrical power to the affected area if it is safe to reach the switch.
Take a head count at the assembly point and report missing persons to the fire team.
Keep the area closed until the fire team declares it safe; check for hidden embers and smoke damage.
Get the electrical installation inspected before re-energising.
Refill or replace any used extinguishers.

MEDICAL.text: Call the emergency team / ambulance and the site first-aider.
If the person is not breathing, start CPR if trained and use the nearest AED.
Do not move the injured person unless they are in immediate danger.
Give first aid within your training: control bleeding with firm pressure, cool burns with running water.
Stay with the person and keep them warm and calm until help arrives.
Make the cause of the injury safe (e.g. dry the wet floor, guard the machine) to protect others.
Inform the person's supervisor and HR, and record treatment given.
Arrange a medical check-up even for minor injuries before the person returns to work.

WATER.text: Isolate the water supply valve feeding the leak.
Switch off electrical equipment and sockets in the wet area if it is safe to do so.
Cordon off the wet area and place wet-floor signs to prevent slips.
Move documents, IT equipment and stock away from the water.
Mop up or pump out standing water and dry the area.
Ask maintenance to repair the source of the leak and inspect nearby pipes or roof sections.
Check ceilings, walls and electrical fittings for water damage before reuse.
Watch for mould or odour over the next days and log any follow-up repairs.

ELECTRICAL.text: Do not touch the person or equipment if there may be live current; switch off power at the source.
Keep everyone away from sparking or exposed wiring; cordon the area.
Anyone who received a shock must get a medical check, even if they feel fine.
Call a licensed electrician to inspect and repair before re-energising.
Apply lockout/tagout on the affected circuit until repairs are done.
For a power outage, check critical loads (servers, cold storage, safety systems) and switch to backup power if available.
Check for burning smell or heat at panels; keep a CO2 extinguisher nearby.

HAZMAT.text: Evacuate people from the area, moving upwind of the release.
Eliminate ignition sources: no switches, phones or flames near a gas leak.
Shut the gas or chemical supply valve if it can be done safely.
Ventilate the area by opening doors and windows if safe.
Only trained responders with the right PPE should contain the spill using spill kits.
Check the substance's safety data sheet (SDS) for exposure first aid and handling.
Send anyone with symptoms (coughing, irritation, dizziness) for medical attention.
Dispose of contaminated material as hazardous waste and record the quantity released.

EQUIPMENT.text: Stop the equipment using the emergency stop and keep people clear.
Apply lockout/tagout before anyone inspects or repairs the equipment.
Inform maintenance with the equipment ID and a description of the fault.
Check for secondary hazards: leaks, overheating, smoke or loose parts.
Notify the production supervisor of the impact and switch to backup equipment if available.
Do not restart until the equipment is repaired and tested.
Record the failure for the maintenance history and root-cause analysis.

SECURITY.text: Do not confront the suspect; move to a safe place and inform security.
If anyone is hurt or threatened, call the emergency team / police.
Preserve the scene: do not touch or move items the suspect handled.
Secure CCTV footage and access-control logs for the time of the incident.
Note a description of the suspect and the direction they went.
List stolen or damaged items with asset tags and estimated value.
Inform the police and file a complaint for theft or assault.
Review and fix the access weakness (door, gate, badge) that allowed the incident.

STRUCTURAL.text: Keep people away and cordon off the damaged area.
If anyone is trapped (e.g. in a lift), call the emergency team and do not attempt an unsafe rescue.
Place warning signs for slip or trip hazards and clean or fix them promptly.
Clear broken glass or debris with gloves and proper tools.
Ask facilities/civil engineering to assess structural safety before reuse.
For lift faults, take the lift out of service and call the lift maintenance contractor.
Photograph the damage for the record and insurance.

ENVIRONMENTAL.text: Stop the source of the release if it is safe to do so.
Block nearby drains with drain covers or absorbent booms to stop spread.
Contain and absorb the spill with a spill kit; keep it away from soil and water.
Inform the environment/EHS officer; check if regulatory reporting is required.
Collect contaminated material and dispose of it as hazardous waste.
Estimate and record the quantity released and the affected area.
Find and fix the cause (leaking container, faulty valve, wrong disposal).

VEHICLE.text: Stop all vehicle movement in the area and switch off the involved vehicles.
If a person was hit, call the emergency team and give first aid; do not move them unless in danger.
Cordon off the area and redirect traffic.
Check for fuel or battery leaks and fire risk.
Record vehicle IDs, driver details and take photos before moving vehicles.
Inspect damaged racks or structures before use (forklift impacts).
Remove the vehicle from service until inspected; review driver training and route markings.

OTHER.text: Make the area safe and keep people away from any hazard.
Inform your supervisor and the EHS team.

GENERAL.text: Inform your supervisor and the EHS team about this incident.
Preserve evidence: photos, CCTV, and do not disturb the scene unnecessarily.
Collect witness statements while details are fresh.
Schedule a root-cause review and track corrective actions to closure.
